sections.title: A) RELATIVE CLAUSES
sections.subtitle: Who, which, that, whose, whom, where, when, why · defining vs non-defining

blocks.heading: Pronombres relativos
blocks.rule: Introducen una oración que da información sobre un sustantivo.

rows: She's the woman **who** bought our car.
They've got a car **which** runs on electricity.
The film **that** I saw was great.
She's the woman **whose** son bought our car.
The person **to whom** this letter is addressed...
This is the town **where** I grew up.
Sunday is a day **when** many people relax.
There's no reason **why** you should worry.

blocks.heading: DEFINING relative clauses (especificativas)
blocks.rule: Dicen DE QUÉ persona o cosa hablamos: son esenciales. Sin comas. Se puede usar that. Si el relativo es OBJETO (detrás hay otro sujeto), se puede omitir; when y why también se pueden omitir.
examples: The couple **who brought me up** were not my real parents.
The people **(who) I know best** are my close friends.
The DVD **(that) you gave me** is fantastic.
2009 was the year **(when) she left university**.

wrong.bad: The man called you is my boss.
wrong.good: The man who called you is my boss. (who es sujeto: no se omite)

blocks.heading: NON-DEFINING relative clauses (explicativas)
blocks.rule: Añaden información EXTRA: la frase se entiende sin ellas. Siempre con comas. Nunca that. El relativo nunca se omite.
examples: The hotel, **which has a hundred bedrooms**, is on the outskirts of the city.
My brother, **who lives in Paris**, is coming to visit.

compare.label: Defining · ¿cuál?
compare.text: My sister **who lives in Rome** is a doctor. (tengo varias hermanas)

compare.label: Non-defining · info extra
compare.text: My sister, **who lives in Rome**, is a doctor. (solo tengo una)

wrong.bad: Avatar, that is my favourite film, was great.
wrong.good: Avatar, which is my favourite film, was great.

blocks.heading: Comment clauses: , WHICH + comentario sobre toda la frase
blocks.rule: Which puede referirse a TODA la oración anterior para comentarla.
examples: It had been raining for 24 hours, **which is why** I didn't go out.
We were stuck in traffic for ages, **which I found really frustrating**.
He refused to apologise, **which made things worse**.

wrong.bad: He didn't call me, what really annoyed me.
wrong.good: He didn't call me, which really annoyed me.

blocks.heading: Preposición + WHOM / WHICH (formal) vs preposición al final (informal)

compare.label: Formal (Writing)
compare.text: Peter is the colleague **on whom** I rely most. · The hotel **in which** we stayed was lovely.

compare.label: Informal (Speaking)
compare.text: Peter is the colleague **(who) I rely on** most. · The hotel **(that) we stayed in** was lovely.

blocks.rule: Cuantificador + of whom / of which: some of whom, most of which, none of whom, the best of which...
examples: He has three sons, **all of whom** are doctors.
She exhibited some photos, **the best of which** was taken in South Africa.

wrong.bad: The man to who I spoke was helpful.
wrong.good: The man to whom I spoke was helpful. (tras preposición: whom)

sections.title: B) PARTICIPLE CLAUSES
sections.subtitle: V-ing · V-ed · Having + participio para unir ideas de forma concisa

blocks.heading: Las tres formas

rows: activo · al mismo tiempo / justo después / razón
**Concentrating** on my work, I didn't realise how late it was.
activo · ANTES de la acción principal / razón
**Having finished** his speech, he left the room.
**Seen** from a distance, the Pyramids look quite small.

blocks.tip: Regla de oro: el sujeto del participio tiene que ser el MISMO que el de la oración principal.

blocks.heading: ¡El sujeto tiene que ser el mismo! (dangling participles)
blocks.rule: Si el sujeto no coincide, la frase dice algo absurdo. Es uno de los errores más penalizados en Writing.

wrong.bad: Walking down the street, the rain started.
wrong.good: Walking down the street, I got caught in the rain. (yo caminaba)

wrong.bad: Having graduated from university, it is easier to find a job.
wrong.good: Having graduated from university, young people find it easier to get a job.

wrong.bad: Studied in detail, you will find this topic fascinating.
wrong.good: Studied in detail, this topic proves fascinating. (el tema es lo estudiado)

blocks.heading: Sustituir conjunciones: because, as, while, when, after, if...

compare.label: Because / as (razón)
compare.text: Because I wanted to pass... → **Wanting** to pass the test, I studied a lot.

compare.label: While (simultáneo)
compare.text: While I was driving home... → **Driving** home, I saw an accident.

compare.label: And (secuencia inmediata)
compare.text: I opened the door and saw a parcel. → **Opening** the door, I saw a parcel.

compare.label: After (anterior)
compare.text: After I had applied... → **Having applied** for the job, I waited for a call.

compare.label: If (pasivo)
compare.text: If it is eaten in small quantities... → **Eaten** in small quantities, chocolate is good for you.

compare.label: Negativa
compare.text: Because I didn't know what to do... → **Not knowing** what to do, I called my mother.

blocks.heading: Con conjunciones y preposiciones
blocks.formula: after / before / while / when / since / instead of / without + V-ING
blocks.rule: Podemos mantener la conjunción para que el significado quede claro. En este caso la oración de participio puede ir al final.
examples: **After watching** that film, I was too scared to go to bed.
She became interested in art **while travelling** in Italy.
You can take the train **instead of catching** the bus.

blocks.heading: En lugar de relative clauses (reduced relative clauses)
formulas: sustantivo + V-ING (= who / which + verbo activo)
sustantivo + V-ED (= who / which + be + participio)
blocks.rule: Quitamos el relativo (y be). V-ing si el significado es activo; V-ed si es pasivo.
examples: There are three pictures **hanging on the wall**. (= which are hanging)
I noticed a man **wearing a suit** and **carrying a large box**.
Anyone **caught shoplifting** will be prosecuted. (= who is caught)
I've brought you some jam **made by my mother**. (= which was made)
blocks.tip: V-ing en lugar de una relativa funciona con estados o acciones en curso, no con una acción única y terminada: The man who won the race (✗ the man winning the race).

blocks.heading: Tras verbos de percepción: see / hear / watch / notice / find + objeto + V-ing
examples: I **found Peter cheating** in the exam.
I **heard someone knocking** at the door.
We **watched children opening** the lock gates.

sections.title: C) APPOSITION
sections.subtitle: Dos sustantivos juntos: el segundo identifica o describe al primero

blocks.heading: ¿Qué es la aposición?
blocks.rule: Es como una relativa non-defining sin who / which + be. Muy útil en Writing para dar información de forma concisa.

compare.label: Relative clause
compare.text: Madrid, **which is the capital of Spain**, is very populous.

compare.label: Apposition
compare.text: Madrid, **the capital of Spain**, is very populous.

blocks.heading: Defining (sin comas) vs non-defining (con comas)

compare.label: Sin comas · dice quién
compare.text: Her friend **Klaus** is a computer engineer. (tiene varios amigos)

compare.label: Con comas · info extra
compare.text: I'm going to see Bev Jackson, **my maths tutor**, this afternoon.

examples: Bob Marley, **a Jamaican singer**, recorded the best-selling reggae album of all time.
The novelist **Zadie Smith** gave a talk.

speaking.structure: In the first picture we can see a [person] [V-ing]..., whereas the second shows a [person] who is [V-ing]...
speaking.example: In the first picture we can see a girl working as a waitress, whereas the second shows a boy who is studying for an exam.
speaking.translation: En la primera foto vemos a [persona] [haciendo algo], mientras que la segunda muestra a [persona] que está [haciendo algo].

speaking.structure: Wanting to [goal], people nowadays tend to [action].
speaking.example: Wanting to save money, people nowadays tend to buy second-hand clothes.
speaking.translation: Queriendo [objetivo], la gente hoy en día tiende a [acción].

speaking.structure: Having [past participle], [people] find it much easier to [action].
speaking.example: Having graduated from university, young people usually find it much easier to get a well-paid job.
speaking.translation: Tras haber [participio], a [la gente] le resulta mucho más fácil [acción].

speaking.structure: [Fact], which is why / which means that [consequence].
speaking.example: Many people work from home now, which means that city centres are much quieter.
speaking.translation: [Hecho], razón por la cual / lo que significa que [consecuencia].

speaking.structure: [Option], seen from a [economic / social] point of view, would be [adjective].
speaking.example: The second option, seen from an economic point of view, would be far more sustainable.
speaking.translation: [Opción], vista desde un punto de vista [económico / social], sería [adjetivo].
